title: Exploring the Structure and Defects in MnCuSiTe, a Multiferroic System using Electron Microscopy
content: Multiferroic materials are class of materials that exhibit the coexistence of at least two ordered states, such as magnetic, electric, or piezo-elastic phases [1]. These materials have garnered significant attention due to the coupling between ferroelectric and magnetic order, enabling novel functionalities such as utilization of electric field to control magnetic properties [2]. This class of materials are ideal candidates for applications such as non-volatile memory, sensors, spintronic devices, and more [2,3]. The known multiferroic systems include BiFeO3, Fe2Mo3O8, LuFeO3/Lu2FeO4 and many others [4,5]. However, incorporating these materials into devices remains challenging due to the disappearance of ferroelectric order at the nanoscale regime [6]. To address these challenges, efforts are underway to discover layered multiferroic materials. This study focuses on a layered transition metal chalcogenide with CuMnSiTe composition.
